title: Rational Numbers
description: Class 7 IMO — Rational numbers: definition and standard form, comparison and ordering, representation on the number line, the four operations, and their properties.

topics.title: Definition & Standard Form
topics.concept: A rational number can be written as p/q where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0. In standard form the denominator is positive and the fraction is in its simplest form: 6/−8 = −3/4.

examples.solution: Make the denominator positive and simplify: −6/8 = −3/4.

recap: Standard form: positive denominator, simplest form.

topics.title: Comparison & the Number Line
topics.concept: Rational numbers can be placed on a number line, with negatives to the left of 0. To compare, a number further to the right is greater, so −2/3 is greater than −3/4. Between any two rational numbers there are many more.

examples.solution: −2/3 is closer to 0, so it is greater.

examples.problem: Name a rational number between 0 and 1.

recap: Further right on the number line means greater.
There are infinitely many rationals between any two.

quiz.q: Which is greater, ⅗ or ⅔?

quiz.explanation: −½ is to the left of ½, so it is smaller.

topics.title: Operations & Properties
topics.concept: To add or subtract rationals, use a common denominator. To multiply, multiply across; to divide, multiply by the reciprocal. Rationals follow the same properties as integers, and the additive inverse of a/b is −a/b.
recap: Add/subtract with a common denominator; divide by multiplying by the reciprocal.

questions.q: A rational number p/q must have q ___ ?
questions.explanation: The denominator q must not be 0.
−2/3 is closer to 0, so it is greater.

questions.q: Which is a rational number between 1 and 2?
A jug has ½ L and ¾ L is added. How much is there now?
A recipe needs ⅔ cup of sugar per batch. How much for 3 batches?
